text:
US military spending in 2017 was about 3.1% of GDP, or roughly $600 billion against a GDP of about $19.5 trillion (SIPRI and World Bank figures). The team note's $1.9 trillion (about 10% of GDP) is too high by roughly a factor of three. Depending on how spending is defined, estimates range from about 3.1% to 3.2%.

CONFIDENCE: 91
